dimensions.note: No credential or secret handling. Global args are repo-relative paths, booleans, and binary names; no vault refs are needed.
Structured placeholders throughout ('Scanned {files} file(s) ...', 'Checked {n} pulled extension(s) ...', 'Workflow wiring: {n} finding(s)'). No interpolation and no sensitive values.

walk() tolerates an unreadable directory; unreadable source files are skipped as a best-effort scan; checkExtensions verifies declared additionalFiles on disk. The new workflow-wiring checks record a failed swamp/health probe as an explicit ok=false detail rather than treating it as a clean result, and Deno.Command failures are converted into that detail.

repo_doctor_test.ts now covers the new wiring helpers: shellWords, extractScriptPaths, normalizePath, resolveScriptPath, inspectScript, extractShellInvocations, declaredScheduleOf, diffSchedules, parseWorkflowSearchJson, and parseServeHealthJson, in addition to the existing path/report/extension parsers. The orchestration methods (scan/checkWorkflowWiring against live git/gh/swamp) remain integration-tested by the workflow rather than unit-tested.
Read-only checks; reruns are idempotent and overwrite the *-current snapshots. scan() writes outputs only after the checks complete, so a thrown check does not expose a half-written combined report.

No external HTTP API. The workflow-wiring check parses swamp CLI JSON and a local serve /health response; malformed JSON is caught and recorded as an explicit failure detail, and non-array/irregular schedule entries are skipped rather than assumed.
Deno.readDir/readFile/stat and awaited Deno.Command.output() only; pipes are drained and no temp files or long-lived handles are created.

src/repo_doctor_test.ts:243-246 embeds the real personal path /var/home/matt/dev/myswamp in a workflow-command fixture. Use a generic placeholder such as /home/user/repo or /work/repo. Non-blocking: test-only, but it is published source and this release introduced it.
All schemas are plain z.object(...) with no .passthrough(); the new WorkflowWiringReportSchema, ScriptInfo, WorkflowSchedule, and ScheduleDiff schemas follow the same pattern.
Every resource and the report file set lifetime 7d and garbageCollection 10, appropriate for a periodic health snapshot.
Not a CRUD lifecycle model: it is an analysis scanner with no create/update/delete surface.
No mutating methods, so no pre-flight gate is required.

scan() writes scan-current, paths-current, extensions-current, gitignore-current, scaffolding-current, workflow-wiring-current, and report-current; each is unique per spec and also written by the single-check methods.
Stateless; reads no stored swamp resources and uses no dataRepository access.
Bumped to 2026.10.23.1 with a no-op upgrades entry for the workflow-wiring check and its workflowDirs/swampBin globals, on top of the 2026.10.21.1 entry.

mechanical.schema-write-conformance: pass — all writeResource payloads match their specs: scan, paths, extensions, gitignore, scaffolding, and workflowWiring populate every declared field, including the new scripts/schedules/liveSource and per-script exec/shebang fields. No placeholder writes.
mechanical.truncation-honesty: pass — no pagination or result caps; each check processes all files/findings, and command output is parsed without silently truncating the finding list.
mechanical.instance-name-consistency: pass — one writer per instance name, with stable *-current names shared by scan and the individual check methods using the same schema.
mechanical.schema-field-coverage: pass — every schema field has a producing path, including workflow-wiring's scripts, schedules, liveSource, and diffSchedules output, plus all Finding fields.
